title: feat: covering tests before a PR, and PRs open with no yes
headline: Before a PR only the tests that cover the change run locally and CI runs the rest; auto-fix gathers every comment first and fixes each class at its root; and a feature branch's PR opens with no yes.
alignment: v1.32.0 lands the rows the kit found on itself about local test runs and the review loop, each reproduced on the released 1.31.0 first, and the owner's two rulings of 2026-11-15.

items.text: A push of a feature branch and opening its PR need no yes: the guard lets one plain gh pr create through, from a feature branch, in a repo whose one remote is origin. Merge, release, tags and main still ask.
items.where: Opening a PR from a pushed feature branch
items.before: The owner's yes in a pop-up
items.after: Opened, then the owner is told

items.text: The kit's test runner prints a notice on a full local run: CI runs the suite on every PR and push, and a change takes the changed run.

One local-test rule: before a PR, run the tests covering the change, and CI's run on the push is the gate; with no CI on the PR the full suite runs once locally. The test-first, loop, team build and PR body texts agree.
items.before: The full suite, then CI again
items.after: The covering tests; CI runs the rest

items.text: Auto-fix gathers every CI failure and review comment first, fixes each class once at its root, runs the covering tests and pushes once; every CI failure gets fixed, with no cap, and a branch has one sweep.
items.before: A fix and a push per comment
items.after: Every comment, each root once, one push

items.text: The merge gate's disarm refuses a PR number with a leading zero, which turned the PR off but left its push held.

verification: Each code change has a test that fails on the code before it: the PR bound, the leading-zero disarm and the notice; the local-test rows were first reproduced on the released 1.31.0.
Recall on keys v11: candidate median 14, baseline (1.31.0) 13, control 0; on keys v10 before the PR ruling, 14 and 14.

decisions.why: The owner's ruling: every CI failure on a PR gets fixed, and the limit that matters is one sweep per branch, which the kit already holds; a cap counted CI fixes as review loops.
Only one plain gh pr create, on a feature branch, in a repo with origin as its one remote, so it cannot open a PR on another repo or hide a second command.

decisions.decision: The notice never holds a run
decisions.why: A full local run is still right where no CI runs, so the runner tells and the exit code is unchanged.
